subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a new cron-scoped tool policy surface, make cron sessions inherit subagent policy, or rely on the existing per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The fix adds or reinterprets security-sensitive config precedence for scheduled runs, and repository policy sets a high bar for new config surfaces and runtime compatibility changes.

options.title: Add `tools.cron.tools`
options.body: Introduce an explicit cron policy layer with documented precedence and tests for interaction with `toolsAllow` and delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron isolated sessions as covered by the existing subagent policy layer, reducing new config surface but coupling two different runtime scopes.

options.title: No new policy
options.body: Keep only per-job `--tools` and delivery safeguards, accepting that operators must configure each job rather than a system-wide cron deny.

recommendation.title: Add `tools.cron.tools`
recommendation.body: Introduce an explicit cron policy layer with documented precedence and tests for interaction with `toolsAllow` and delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review and recent agent/runtime history make steipete the best available routing owner for the policy choice.
